newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - NOV 4.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - NOV 4.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn does not plan to initiate bilateral talks with his Slovak counterpart, Vladimir Meciar, at the Hungarian-Slovak-Austrian summit in Piestani.
- The Hungarian Socialist Party (MSZP) will submit a proposal to the Parliament for setting up a privatisation committee.
- Several customs officer in Roszke, south Hungary are suspected with having been bribed.
- Member states of Germany are arguing over what should be done with hazardous waste transported to Hungary from Germany.

- It has a significance for the whole region that Romania is not likely to be able to set up a government without RMDSZ, the party of ethnic Hungarians in the country, said politologist Gusztav Molnar.
- Soviet tanks suppressed the Hungarian revolution on November 4, forty years ago.
